measured.note: trace_within_budget_points and trace_over_budget_points are BOTH real byte measurements (trace_status=measured in the sweep). The GEMM n=768 traces are MEASURED over budget (~120-209 MiB > 64 MiB), not timeouts. The ceiling is the largest within-budget trace; every within-budget size is sub-millisecond. Timed-out traces are tracked separately under timed_out_traces with UNMEASURED byte size.

production_duration_reconcile_floor.note: Authoritative dual-source reconcile floor from the committed production cohort (--shape-point + override path): the smallest reconciling cells run several ms (n~2048); a kernel must run >~2-3ms for host enqueue/sync overhead to fall under 5%.

rationale: The NVBit trace is byte-budget-admissible only at small (sub-millisecond) kernels: GEMM variants are within budget at n<=512 (~5-60 MiB) and MEASURED over budget at n=768 (~120-209 MiB > 64 MiB); the attention slugs do not complete a trace at n=512 within the wall cap (timeout, byte size unmeasured). Either way no trace-budget-admissible size exceeds ~512^3, while the CUPTI dual-source duration reconciles only at large (>~2-3ms) kernels. The two size windows are disjoint, so a single (arch, slug, shape_point) cell cannot carry BOTH a trace and a reconciling duration. The per-cell four-source (trace+L1+L2+duration) requirement is therefore unmeetable for the DURATION leg. This is a structural property of the two collection methods, not of the slug set. The >=50-cell cohort proceeds as a BI-label (trace+L1+L2) base; the duration label lives in the SEPARATE duration cohort (sm120_duration_cohort.json) and feeds the duration predictor. The tri-label roster validator stays fail-closed and still reports four-source gaps; this artifact does NOT claim those gaps are satisfied.
timed_out_note: These traces (the attention slugs at n=512) did not complete within the per-trace wall cap; their byte sizes are UNMEASURED and are NOT claimed as measured byte over-budget (distinct from the MEASURED over-budget GEMM n=768 rows above).
